cases.concern: Bash substitution state is sequential inside and isolated outside
Ungated cd failure keeps the incoming cwd reachable
cases.notes: The exact /maybe state is reachable only on cd success; semicolon continuation also includes the unchanged failure state.

cases.concern: Joined cwd clears false path resolution but preserves the dynamic attribution signal
cases.notes: The v0.3 projection removes both false exact resolutions while retaining the established dynamic cwd sentinel for v0.2 consumers.

cases.concern: The last Bash pipeline stage may or may not share parent state
cases.notes: Without locked execution options, lastpipe makes parent-scope leakage conditional and therefore unknown.

cases.concern: Decoded bash -c inherits invocation cwd and isolates inner changes
cases.notes: The wrapper uses invocation state for v0.3 facts while its exit restores the outer state.

cases.concern: A proved empty loop has no state transition
cases.input: for f in; do cd /tmp; done; pwd
cases.notes: The authored body remains structurally visible, but the Never iteration plan contributes no cwd mutation to the following command.

cases.concern: Internal iteration order preserves duplicates independently of the public finite set
cases.input: for f in a b a; do :; done; printf '%s' "$f"
cases.notes: The public loop-body value domain may deduplicate to {a,b}; the private iteration plan still ends in a.

cases.concern: A decoded child process does not receive an unexported loop binding
cases.input: for f in a; do bash -c 'printf "%s" "$f"'; done
cases.notes: Unlike a parenthesized subshell, bash -c receives only proved exported variables; the outer loop binding is not substituted into the child.

cases.concern: A parenthesized subshell inherits shell bindings while isolating exit state
cases.input: for f in a; do (printf "%s" "$f"); done
cases.notes: The subshell receives the loop binding but none of its later mutations can escape back to the loop body.

cases.concern: Dynamic glob covering directory

cases.concern: Literal heredoc data does not create hidden commands or unnecessary approval scope
cases.notes: v0.3 fixes quoted-delimiter adjacency, preserves the literal body as data, and keeps the output path independently policy-relevant.

cases.concern: Static here-string data does not force a raw-command approval prompt
cases.notes: The exact value includes Bash's appended newline; an executable-aware consumer may ignore stdin data only when that data is not policy-sensitive for the receiver.

cases.concern: Unknown stdin data does not make an otherwise complete redirect structurally incomplete
cases.notes: The unknown value is not automatically approval-sensitive for cat, but a consumer can classify the same stdin position as sensitive for an interpreter such as bash.

cases.concern: Escaped variable provenance survives word decoding
cases.notes: The real Bash argv value is the literal relative filename $HOME. The v0.2 parser incorrectly substitutes the configured home directory.

cases.concern: Escaped inline prefix composes with a quoted suffix
cases.notes: Bash passes one native argument containing a literal $HOME.json file reference; the current resolver reports /home/test.json instead.

cases.concern: All-static mixed quoting resolves without DynamicSkip
cases.notes: Both fragments are static. The existing DynamicSkip expectation in executable corpus case 166 is an approval-fatigue workaround for lost provenance, not the desired v0.3 result.

cases.concern: Escape provenance survives within one double-quoted token
Literal and expandable regions compose within one token
Runtime special parameter punctuation cannot become a glob path
cases.notes: The released parser mistakes runtime $? punctuation for a quoted glob.

cases.concern: Runtime positional parameters cannot become literal paths
cases.notes: The positional value depends on the runtime invocation and cannot be treated as the filename $1.

cases.concern: Quoted dollar-at can produce zero or multiple arguments
cases.notes: Quoted $@ has runtime-dependent cardinality, so one authored token cannot be claimed as one exact path.

cases.concern: An outer closing quote does not complete an open braced interpolation
cases.notes: Real Bash rejects this syntax; no exact or compatibility path may be exposed.

cases.concern: Adjacent escaped and quoted redirect fragments form one target
cases.notes: The released parser resolves the $HOME prefix as the redirect and emits the quoted suffix as an unrelated argument.

cases.concern: Bash does not interpret an unquoted PowerShell provider-looking prefix
cases.notes: The shared v0.2 resolver incorrectly strips a PowerShell provider prefix from Bash argv.
